question: May a Florida notary solemnize a marriage?

options.why: Correct. Florida is one of the few states whose notaries may perform marriage ceremonies.
Wrong. That's the rule in Texas, New York and California, but Florida notaries may solemnize marriages.
Wrong. A judge isn't needed; the notary officiates on their own.
Wrong. The power applies anywhere in Florida.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Solemnizing Marriages (p. 17)

question: Before a Florida notary solemnizes a marriage, the couple must present:

options.why: Correct. A Florida license issued by a county court clerk is required before the ceremony.
Wrong. Birth certificates don't replace the marriage license.
Wrong. A Florida ceremony requires a Florida marriage license.
Wrong. Officiating without a license is improper.

explanation: A valid Florida marriage license is required.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Solemnizing Marriages: license requirement (p. 18)

question: May a Florida notary solemnize their own marriage?

options.why: Correct. A notary may not officiate a marriage in which they are one of the parties.
Wrong. Officiating your own wedding is a conflict; the notary is a party.
Wrong. Witnesses don't cure the notary being a party.
Wrong. The method doesn't matter; the notary can't officiate their own marriage.

explanation: A notary may not solemnize their own marriage.

question: What is an 'attested photocopy' in Florida?

options.text: A copy the notary supervised or made from an original and attests is true and complete
options.why: Correct. §117.05(12) lets notaries attest photocopies of non-public-record originals.

options.text: A copy of a birth certificate
options.why: Wrong. Vital records are excluded from notary photocopy attestation.

options.text: Any document the signer copied at home
options.why: Wrong. The notary must make or supervise the copy from the original.

options.text: A copy of a recorded deed
options.why: Wrong. Public records come from their custodian.

explanation: A notary may attest a photocopy made from an original that isn't a public or vital record.

question: May a Florida notary attest a photocopy of a birth certificate?

options.text: No; certified copies of vital records come from the issuing agency
options.why: Correct. Vital and public records are excluded from notary attestation.
Wrong. Vital records are expressly excluded.

options.text: Yes, if the original is shown
options.why: Wrong. Even with the original, vital records are excluded.
Wrong. No fee changes the exclusion, and $25 is the online fee.

explanation: Vital records can't be attested by a notary.

question: A signer can't write and signs by mark. What does Florida require?

options.text: The mark is made in the presence of the notary and two disinterested witnesses, and the notary writes the person's name near the mark
options.why: Correct. That is the statutory procedure for signature by mark.
Wrong. Two disinterested witnesses are required.
Wrong. Florida requires two.
Wrong. That's a different procedure, for people physically unable to sign or make a mark.

explanation: A signature by mark needs two disinterested witnesses and notation by the notary.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Signature by mark (p. 16)

question: A person physically unable to sign or make a mark asks the notary to sign for them. What does Florida allow?

options.text: The notary may sign the person's name at their direction and in their presence, and notes that the signature was affixed by the notary under §117.05(14)
options.why: Correct. The statute allows this with a specific notation.
Wrong. The statute provides a procedure for this situation.
Wrong. The statute authorizes the notary, not a relative.
Wrong. The document still needs a signature made under the statutory procedure.

explanation: Florida notaries may sign for a physically unable person under §117.05(14), with the required notation.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Signing for a person with a disability (p. 17)

question: Before notarizing for a blind signer, what must a Florida notary do?

options.text: Read the document to the signer
options.why: Correct. §117.05(14) requires the notary to read the document to a blind signer before notarizing.
Wrong. The statute adds the step of reading the document aloud.
Wrong. No doctor's note is required.
Wrong. Blind signers may be served once the document has been read to them.

explanation: A notary must read the document to a blind signer before notarizing.

question: Which vehicle-related task may a Florida notary perform?

options.text: Verify a vehicle identification number (VIN) on the state form
options.why: Correct. Florida notaries may verify VINs for DHSMV purposes.
Wrong. Titles come from the tax collector or DHSMV.
Wrong. Registration is done by the tax collector.
Wrong. Not a notarial function.

source: Fla. Stat. §319.23; Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Vehicle Identification Number verification (p. 19)

question: What is a Florida 'civil-law notary'?

options.text: A Florida attorney with at least five years of practice appointed by the Secretary of State with broader authentication powers
options.why: Correct. Civil-law notaries are a separate office under chapter 118.
Wrong. Language skills have nothing to do with the office.
Wrong. That's the online notary bond.
Wrong. That's exactly the confusion the advertising rules prevent.

explanation: Civil-law notaries are experienced Florida attorneys appointed under chapter 118.

question: Who issues apostilles for Florida-notarized documents?

options.why: Correct. The Florida Department of State issues apostilles authenticating Florida notaries.
Wrong. A notary can't authenticate their own authority.
Wrong. Florida has no county-clerk step for apostilles.
Wrong. The U.S. Department of State handles federal documents, not state notarizations.

explanation: The Florida Department of State issues apostilles.

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Apostille Certification (p. 26)

question: Where may a Florida notary perform marriages?

options.why: Correct. Like other notarial acts, the power is statewide.
Wrong. Not limited to a county.
Wrong. Florida authority ends at the state line.
Wrong. No venue restriction.

explanation: Florida notaries may perform marriages anywhere in Florida.

question: Can a Florida notary act as a witness to a will and also notarize the self-proving affidavit?

options.text: A notary may notarize the self-proving affidavit, but a non-attorney notary should not supervise will execution or advise on it
options.why: Correct. Notarizing is fine; supervising or advising is the practice of law.
Wrong. Notarizing the affidavit is a normal notarial act.

options.text: The notary must draft the will
options.why: Wrong. Drafting is the practice of law.

options.text: The notary must keep the will
options.why: Wrong. Notaries don't keep documents.

explanation: Notarizing the self-proof is fine; advising or supervising is legal practice.
source: Fla. Stat. §732.503; Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Duties of Notaries (p. 13)

question: A hospitalized patient is drowsy and confused. The family insists. The notary should:

options.text: Decline or reschedule until the signer is alert and understands
options.why: Correct. §117.107 bars notarizing for someone who appears mentally incapable of understanding.
Wrong. That risks abuse of a vulnerable signer.
Wrong. The signer must act personally, and family may be interested parties.
Wrong. Witnesses don't cure incapacity.

explanation: Don't proceed if the signer lacks understanding.

question: A Florida notary is in Georgia and is asked to notarize under the Florida commission. The notary should:

options.text: Decline; a Florida commission authorizes acts only within Florida (online notaries must also be physically in Florida)
options.why: Correct. Authority is territorial for both traditional and online acts.
Wrong. No authority in Georgia.
Wrong. Florida online notaries must be physically in Florida.
Wrong. That records an act outside the notary's jurisdiction.

explanation: Florida notaries must be in Florida to act.

question: What should a notary do when asked to notarize a photograph?

options.text: Notarize a signer's written, signed statement about the photo, not the photo itself
options.why: Correct. Notaries certify signatures and oaths, not images.
Wrong. That certifies nothing meaningful.
Wrong. Notaries can't vouch for images.
Wrong. A signed statement about the photo can be notarized.

explanation: Notarize a signed statement, not an image.

question: Does a Florida notary need to keep a copy of the marriage certificate?

options.text: Not required, but the license and certificate must be completed and returned to the issuing clerk
options.why: Correct. The officiant completes the certificate and returns it to the clerk.
Wrong. Notaries don't need to keep or notarize a copy.
Wrong. The license must be completed and returned.
Wrong. It goes to the issuing clerk.

explanation: The officiant completes and returns the license and certificate to the clerk of court.
source: Fla. Stat. ch. 741; Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries

refs.title: Governor's Reference Manual for Notaries: Solemnizing Marriages: completing the marriage record (p. 18)

question: Which act may a Florida notary perform?

options.why: Correct. Administering oaths is a core notarial power under §117.03.
Wrong. Only the Department of State issues apostilles.
Wrong. Recording is done by the clerk of court.
Wrong. Only courts can grant divorces.

explanation: Administering oaths is a core notarial power.
